headlines.title: American Express (AXP) Stock May Sit Below Fair Value As AML Fine Lands
headlines.summary: American Express has delivered a 107.6% share price gain over the past three years, even as the last year has been softer, and that raises a simple question for you as an investor. Is the current price still supported by what the company actually earns on the capital it puts to work in its business? A 107.6% three year return puts real pressure on the idea that American Express's share price is still in line with the returns it earns on its capital.

headlines.title: Amex ‘Proof of Intent’: The Issuer Side Enters the Agentic Checkout Wars
headlines.summary: Amex's "Proof of Intent" token is the sixth definition of "agentic checkout" and the first from the issuer side. It moves the evidence issuers hold, not the merchant-of-record loss default.

headlines.title: American Express (AXP): Double-Digit Growth at a Below-Average Multiple
headlines.summary: American Express (NYSE:AXP) raised its full-year revenue outlook in its most recent quarterly report. Since then, the stock has cooled off instead of celebrating. That disconnect is the whole story. Most people know Amex as the card you see at business dinners and in airport lounges. Behind it sits an unusual model.

headlines.title: American Express Publishes Intent Intelligence Framework for Trusted Agentic Commerce
headlines.summary: NEW YORK, October 13, 2026--American Express today published its Intent Intelligence framework, detailing the company’s recommended approach to capturing and authenticating a customer’s purchase intent before an AI agent completes a transaction. The framework then preserves that intent as a control throughout the transaction lifecycle. By making its framework publicly available, American Express aims to help advance a common industry approach for intent in agentic commerce.

headlines.title: Amex introduces a framework to prevent AI agents from making unauthorized purchases
headlines.summary: American Express is introducing a new framework designed to ensure AI agents only make purchases their users have authorized, potentially preventing costly mistakes and disputes as AI-powered shopping grows.

description: American Express Company, together with its subsidiaries, operates as an integrated payments company in the United States, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, the Asia Pacific, Australia, New Zealand, Latin America, Canada, the Caribbean, and internationally. It operates through four segments: U.S. Consumer Services, Commercial Services, International Card Services, and Global Merchant and Network Services. The company offers credit and charge cards and complementary products and services, including travel, dining, and lifestyle and expense management products and services; and banking and other payment and financing products and services, including deposits and non-card lending. It also provides merchant acquisition and processing, servicing and settlement, fraud prevention, and point-of-sale marketing and information products and services, as well as network services. The company offers its products and services to consumers, small businesses, mid-sized companies, and large corporations through mobile and online applications, affiliate marketing, customer referral programs, third-party service providers and business partners, in-house sales teams, direct mail, telephone, and direct response advertising. American Express Company was founded in 1850 and is headquartered in New York, New York.
